Maintenance Report — MNT-0037-001

Asset: WELL-0037 (SW-23 Well 037, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 05 Nov 2022 08:00 · Finished: 22 Nov 2022 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 410 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0037-0003 on 2022-11-03 Report written: 24 Nov 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0037-0003 showed the wellhead at 22.6 °C with the air at 18.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Total21,535

Notes and recommendations

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0037-006

Asset: WELL-0037 (SW-23 Well 037, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 28 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Jul 2023 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 29 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0037-0041 on 2023-07-27 Report written: 30 Jul 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0037-0041 at 07:00 on 2023-07-27 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.6% of the pad area, estimated 0.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 229 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 183 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0037-006 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0037-021

Asset: WELL-0037 (SW-23 Well 037, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 20 Jul 2025 08:00 · Finished: 23 Jul 2025 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 72 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0037-0141 on 2025-07-17 Report written: 23 Jul 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0037-0141 showed the wellhead at 35.3 °C with the air at 33.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

  • About 2.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0037-026; the manifest was only completed the following week (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.44% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
